title: paged KV cache: block allocator reuse and pinning optimizations
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: reduce allocation churn and tail latency in the paged KV cache by reusing block allocator state, improving pinning semantics to avoid premature evictions, and tightening the eviction heuristics used by the block manager. Summary: this PR introduces a reusable allocator pool for fixed-size KV blocks, changes pinning to be reference-count-based with explicit pin timeouts, and updates the eviction policy to prefer cold blocks with no recent KV hits and no active pins. The change reduces GC-like compaction events and reduces mutex contention during high-concurrency continuous-batching workloads. Implementation highlights: 1) a BlockAllocatorPool that keeps recently freed blocks in per-thread local caches and a global shared pool; 2) BlockPin becomes a lightweight RAII-style token (C++/Rust interop) with explicit TryPin/Unpin APIs and an optional timeout overwrite for long-running calls; 3) EvictionPolicy gains a short-circuit fast-path to skip pinned blocks and rank candidates by recency and reuse-score; 4) improved accounting and metrics (kv.block_reuse_count, kv.pin_conflicts, kv.eviction_skipped_pinned) and new unit/integration tests that exercise high-concurrency pin/unpin scenarios; 5) careful deterministic teardown to avoid pool leaks during process exit and private deployments. Backwards compatibility: public APIs are unchanged; internal behavior is opt-in via a config flag runtime.paged_kv.enable_allocator_reuse=true which defaults to true after canary. Testing & CI: added microbenchmarks showing throughput gains and tail latency reductions; existing tests updated to account for pin semantics. Rollout plan: staged canary (10% nodes) for 48h observing kv_cache_miss_rate, kv.pin_conflicts, and latency P99; if stable, roll to 50% then 100%. Related work: follows up on prior paged-kv PRs (pr-23891, pr-22456) and ties to ENG-4821. Results: internal canary shows ~12% throughput improvement on chat workloads, ~18% reduction in P99 token latency, and ~25% reduction in pause time caused by block scans. No breaking API changes. See release_notes for operational guidance.
commits: Add TryPin/Unpin token and timeout handling
EvictionPolicy: skip pinned blocks and add reuse-score ranking
Add unit and integration tests for concurrent pin/unpin and eviction
Docs: runtime config and rollout guidance
review_comments: Diego: Nice work. Please add a test that simulates long-running pins overlapping with eviction windows; ensure there is no starvation.
Ava: added long-running pin test in test_block_allocator.cc and documented the expected behavior in ops doc.
Priya: Can you clarify memory accounting when allocator pool grows under transient load? Is there a hard cap?
Ava: pool has a soft cap per-thread and a global upper bound guarded by atomic counters; added comments and a config runtime.paged_kv.pool_size_cap.
Ethan: Benchmarks look promising; can we add a canary rollout plan and metrics to track?
Ava: included rollout plan in PR description and added kv.pin_conflicts and kv.block_reuse_count metrics for monitoring.
release_notes: Performance: Paged KV cache allocator reuse and improved pinning semantics reduce allocation churn and tail latency; expect ~10-15% throughput improvement on cont-batching workloads and lower 99th percentile token latency. Operational: new metrics (kv.block_reuse_count, kv.pin_conflicts, kv.eviction_skipped_pinned) and runtime flags runtime.paged_kv.enable_allocator_reuse and runtime.paged_kv.pool_size_cap. Rollout: canary recommended.
rollout_notes: Canary 10% for 48h; monitor kv_cache_miss_rate, kv.pin_conflicts, kv.eviction_skipped_pinned, latency P99. If stable, promote to 50% for 24h, then 100%.
notes: This PR is follow-up to earlier block allocator improvements (see pr-23891, pr-22456).
Added extra telemetry to detect regression early; hooks are lightweight and default off for private deployments until rollout completes.
